blocks.content:
73rd Amendment – Panchayats (1992)
74th Amendment – Municipalities (1992)
Three-tier rural system
Reservation for women – minimum 1/3
Eleventh Schedule – 29 subjects
Twelfth Schedule – 18 subjects
Tenure – 5 years
Balwant Rai Mehta Committee – 1957

items: Match the Schedule to Subjects: Eleventh Schedule has 29 subjects (Panchayats), whereas Twelfth Schedule has 18 subjects (Municipalities).
Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) is frequently asked as the pioneering committee for the three-tier rural system.
Both 73rd and 74th Amendments were passed in the year 1992.
Remember the constitutional tenure of local bodies is 5 years with a minimum 1/3 reservation for women.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd Amendment (1992) constitutionalized Panchayats and introduced the Eleventh Schedule containing 29 subjects.
The 74th Amendment (1992) constitutionalized Municipalities and introduced the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects.
Rural local governance follows a three-tier system with a mandatory 5-year tenure.
A minimum of 1/3 of all seats are reserved for women in local self-government bodies.
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was formed in 1957 to recommend the Panchayati Raj framework.
